messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
please help me get a usable prompt for cleaning up the ortiz family photo catalogue, not a history of the family and not captions from scratch. my aunt mara has been assembling it with her brother daniel from sixteen scans of prints that were in two albums and a small envelope. the records already have IDs F01 through F16 and those IDs matter because the relatives use them when they talk about a picture. keep the catalogue entries recognizable and keep any names, places, captions, and notes that are actually supplied. some of the handwriting is hard to read, so it shouldn't turn a guess into a fact.

the album pages were scanned in the order mara found them, and the envelope pictures were placed after those pages when the files were made. the current order is therefore a scan order, not a family timeline. the pictures cover several parts of the family, including the ortiz relatives around tacoma and yakima, and the liu relatives who later lived in salinas and portland. those place names appear inconsistently in the notes; sometimes a note gives a town, sometimes it only says who is in the picture. don't treat the location as proof of when the photo was taken, or assume that people stayed in one town for a whole decade.

what i need is a decision rule for arranging the existing catalogue. check the date evidence for every one of the sixteen records. a date counts as supported only when the record has an exact date written on the back of the print or an exact date in the scan metadata. don't derive a date from clothing, a building, a holiday, the apparent age of a child, an album page, or a relative's memory. a phrase like “probably 1974” or just “summer” is not an exact date for this purpose. it can stay as a note if it's already in the entry, but it can't make that entry count as dated.

if every record has one of those exact supported dates, then arrange all sixteen entries in chronological order and show each supported date with its entry. if two entries have the same date, leave those entries in their existing scan order relative to each other. the catalogue should still use the F IDs, not new numbering that replaces them. don't put an entry earlier or later based on a guess, and don't upgrade an approximate note into an exact date. i think mara has written some of the dates in the notes field rather than in the heading, so check the whole entry and not just its first line.

if even one of the sixteen records does not have an exact supported date, don't make a chronological catalogue and don't fill in an estimated date for the missing one. do something useful instead: group the existing entries into a small thematic index using only a place or event that is actually stated in that entry. keep the IDs easy to find and keep the original scan order inside each theme. if an entry names no place or event, put it under a neutral “place or event not recorded” heading rather than trying to identify it from the image. this is an alternative arrangement for the catalogue, not a second version after the chronological one.

there are a couple of family notes that should remain ordinary notes, not turn into claims about the dates. mara wrote, “Grandma called these the ferry pictures, though the ferry is only visible in two.” keep that wording if the note appears with an entry, and don't make every picture in that group a ferry photograph. one entry also has a pencilled “maybe Aunt Rosa?” beside a woman whose name isn't certain. retain the uncertainty as written; don't decide that the person is Rosa. the goal is to make the supplied catalogue easier to use, not to settle family disagreements.

1. for the catalogue itself, keep the existing entry information and make the layout clear enough that relatives can scan it on a laptop or print it. use a simple heading for each entry or index group, with the F ID prominent. leave a blank field or wording as it was if the source has no caption or date; don't write a replacement caption to make the entries look finished. spelling can be cleaned only where the intended name or place is unambiguous. please don't silently combine two records because they seem to show the same people.

mara remembers that the envelope was found in a kitchen drawer after the albums came from her mother's house, but that doesn't establish when any print was made. the albums have faded blue covers and one is labeled “Sunday visits”; that label can be retained as an existing album note if it belongs in a record, but it isn't a date source either. the catalogue is for the cousins who are sharing these scans, not for an exhibit, so keep the descriptions plain and useful and avoid writing a family narrative around them.

return only the finished catalogue in the applicable arrangement, with no introduction, explanation of which rule applied, or closing note. if the thematic index is needed, use that instead of adding a chronology or an extra section explaining the missing dates. keep the final output limited to the catalogue material and its headings.", "output": "Please prepare a clear, usable version of the existing Ortiz family photo catalogue. Do not write a family history or create new captions. The catalogue contains sixteen scanned prints assembled by Mara and her brother Daniel from two albums and a small envelope. Keep the existing IDs F01 through F16, since relatives use them to refer to the pictures. Preserve the supplied names, places, captions, and notes, and do not turn uncertain handwriting or guesses into facts.

The album pages were scanned in the order Mara found them, with the envelope pictures placed afterward when the files were made. This is scan order, not a family timeline. The images include Ortiz relatives around Tacoma and Yakima and Liu relatives who later lived in Salinas and Portland. Place names are recorded inconsistently: some entries name a town, while others identify only people. Do not use a location to establish when a photo was taken or assume that anyone stayed in one town throughout a decade.

Check the date evidence in every entry. A date is supported only if an exact date is written on the print’s back or appears in the scan metadata. Do not infer dates from clothing, buildings, holidays, a child’s apparent age, album pages, or family memories. Wording such as “probably 1974” or “summer” may remain as a supplied note, but it does not count as an exact date. Check the whole entry, including the notes field, rather than only its first line.

Apply this arrangement rule:
1. **If all sixteen records have an exact supported date:** arrange the entries chronologically and show each supported date with its entry. Keep entries with the same date in their existing scan order. Retain the F IDs; do not replace them with new numbering. Do not use guesses to place entries or change approximate notes into exact dates.
2. **If even one record lacks an exact supported date:** do not create a chronological catalogue or estimate the missing date. Instead, make a small thematic index using only a place or event stated in an entry. Keep the F IDs easy to find and preserve the original scan order within each theme. Put entries with no stated place or event under “place or event not recorded.” Use this arrangement instead of a chronology; do not provide both.

Keep family notes as notes, not as evidence for dates. If the supplied entry includes Mara’s wording, retain: “Grandma called these the ferry pictures, though the ferry is only visible in two.” Do not imply that every picture in the group shows a ferry. Preserve the pencilled note “maybe Aunt Rosa?” with its uncertainty; do not identify the woman as Rosa. The catalogue should make the supplied material easier to use, not settle family disagreements.

Use clear headings for entries or index groups, with each F ID prominent, so relatives can scan the catalogue on a laptop or print it. Do not replace a missing caption or date with newly written text. Correct spelling only when the intended name or place is unambiguous, and do not combine records because they appear to show the same people.

Mara remembers that the envelope was found in a kitchen drawer after the albums came from her mother’s house, but this does not establish when any print was made. The albums have faded blue covers, and one is labeled “Sunday visits.” Retain that label as an existing album note if it belongs with a record, but do not use it as a date source. Keep descriptions plain and useful for the cousins sharing the scans; do not write an exhibit text or a family narrative.

Return only the finished catalogue in the applicable arrangement. Do not add an introduction, explain which rule applied, or include a closing note. If the thematic index is needed, do not add a chronology or a separate section explaining missing dates. Limit the output to catalogue material and its headings."}]
